clue.text: Is it used to pick out junk in the dark?

definitions.text: Is it used to pick out junk in the dark?

parts.words: Is it used to pick out junk in the dark?
parts.note: junk reads as rubbish, but a junk is also a Chinese sailing boat, so this is a paper lamp from that country that might light one up at night

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what tool helps sort through rubbish at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper lamp of the kind made in China would light up a junk, the Chinese sailing vessel, after dark.

clue.text: Those running on air seem romantic fantasy

indicators.note: a fantasy is a wild invention, so the letters of the words before it are freely reimagined

explanation.surface: Lighthearted people seem caught up in a romantic daydream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running on air' suggests elation, but it means spoken descriptions broadcast on radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast commentaries run on air, describing a match or event live on radio.

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so the letters of the name are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone asks what problem a girl named Susie has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' does double duty in an all-in-one clue: it disturbs the letters of SUSIE and, with the whole clue, describes a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a problem or point of trouble, as in what's the issue.

clue.text: Shown by Shackleton, but not his ship?

definitions.text: Shown by Shackleton, but not his ship?

parts.words: Shown by Shackleton, but not his ship?
parts.note: the polar explorer showed great staying power, and ironically his ship bearing that name was crushed by ice

explanation.surface: A quality displayed by the Antarctic explorer but not by his vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance was crushed in Antarctic pack ice in 1915, though the explorer's own fortitude saved his crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the stamina Shackleton showed, and was also the name of his ship that sank.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters are one possible arrangement of the words before it

explanation.surface: A request to be laid to rest underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Embowel is an archaic verb meaning to enclose deeply or bury within something.

definitions.meaning: lasting and enduring, as in a lasting friendship
putting up with, tolerating, as in cannot stand something

explanation.definitionFit: Abiding means enduring or steadfast, and also tolerating, from abide in its sense of put up with.

clue.text: The art of the con man

definitions.text: The art of the con man

parts.words: The art of the con man
parts.note: a swindler's skill lies in deceiving victims with a dodge or ruse

explanation.surface: A remark about the craft practised by swindlers.
explanation.definitionFit: A deception or ruse is the swindler's stock in trade, the knack of fooling people.

clue.text: Herds free to roam can be renewed

indicators.note: roaming cattle wander about, so the letters of the words before it move freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Cattle released to wander the land are revitalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be refreshed is to be revived or renewed in energy.

parts.note: Clio is one of the nine Muses, the one presiding over history, so she is an example of a muse

explanation.surface: Someone imagines the opinion of a daughter of the Muse of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Clio as one example of a Muse; the 's in Clio's is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder, so mused is the past tense meaning pondered or thought.

definitions.meaning: in Scotland a factor is a land agent or estate steward, a role also filled by these officers
officers of the court who seize goods for unpaid debts

explanation.definitionFit: Bailiffs manage estates as stewards and also seize debtors' property under court orders.

indicators.note: trained means taught to behave differently, so the letters of the words after it are reshaped

explanation.surface: A bird taught to attack another creature with its beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magpie' looks like the bird, but it is the definition in its sense of someone who compulsively takes things.
explanation.definitionFit: A magpie is figuratively a compulsive collector or pilferer, like someone with a pathological urge to steal.

clue.text: It is raised at the start

definitions.text: It is raised at the start

parts.words: It is raised at the start
parts.note: start reads as the beginning, but here it means a jump of surprise, when people lift this feature of the face

explanation.surface: Something is hoisted at the opening of an event, like a curtain or flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising this hairy arch above the eye is the classic gesture of surprise or a sudden start.

parts.note: Indian suggests Native American land, but Indian ink is a writing fluid and reservation can mean a reservoir holding it

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a tract of land set aside for Native Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: The container on an old desk holds a reserve of ink, including the black Indian ink.

indicators.note: nouveau is French for new, so the letters of the neighbouring words are made new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A remark about physical activity within the Art Nouveau design movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art Nouveau' reads as the decorative style, but 'Nouveau' (new) is the anagram signal working on IN and ART.
explanation.definitionFit: To train is to exercise, as athletes do to build fitness.

clue.text: It can give the staff a rating

definitions.text: It can give the staff a rating

parts.words: It can give the staff a rating
parts.note: staff suggests a stick or rod, but here it is a workforce and rating is a judgement of performance

explanation.surface: An object that tells you how highly a stick scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff performance review evaluates employees and gives each a rating.

parts.note: beams suggest the timbers of a vessel, but this anchored vessel matters for the light beams it sends out, while being called light

explanation.surface: A remark that a ship's timber beams matter even so.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored vessel carrying a beacon warns shipping with its beams of light, though its name says it is light.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'A rating for the crew' (9), gives no definition or wordplay for TRANSFORM; it reads like a variant of the 14-down clue, so it may be misplaced or garbled, and no source gives the printed clue.

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
present means here, as in answering a register

explanation.surface: Someone points out a written message at this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to depict or show it, as a painting does.

clue.text: Professors once deserve to be put inside (ie retired)

indicators.note: the word for deserve is placed within the other letters
retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: to merit something is to deserve it

explanation.surface: Elderly academics deserve to be confined, that is, pensioned off.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(ie retired)' looks like an explanatory aside, but it is wordplay; 'Professors once' means professors who have retired.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are retired professors who keep their title in honour, hence professors once active.

indicators.note: made from indicates the letters of the following word are reworked into something new

parts.note: feta is a Greek cheese of sheep or goat milk

explanation.surface: A material produced out of greasy cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from' rearranges FAT to TAF, which is then followed by FETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven cloth, and taffeta is a crisp silk fabric.

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car

explanation.surface: A vintage vehicle that comes with its original stereo.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio means sound, especially recorded or broadcast sound, as in an audio system.

clue.text: Beheaded king, enough of a precedent

indicators.note: a beheaded word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: rex is Latin for king, used in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A decapitated monarch serves as a warning to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beheaded' removes the first letter of REX, leaving EX; 'of a' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An example set earlier serves as a precedent for later cases to follow.

indicators.note: fresh means newly made, so the letters of the word before it are formed anew

explanation.surface: Leftover produce that is still in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pears are a common orchard fruit.

clue.text: Fault is mended in narrow pipe

indicators.note: something mended is put back together, so the letters of the two words are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A defect in a slender tube has been repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine a fistula is an abnormal narrow channel, and the word is Latin for a pipe or tube.

clue.text: The range of half your vocals

indicators.note: half of means the back half of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A singer is told their range is only half what it should be.
explanation.walkthrough: The URALS are a mountain range dividing Europe from Asia; 'range' plays on a singer's vocal range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural Mountains form a long mountain range in Russia.

clue.text: Radioactive element at Etna is volatile

indicators.note: volatile means unstable or explosive, so the letters of the words before it are blown apart and reformed

explanation.surface: A dangerous element is present at Mount Etna, which is a restless volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is volatile' looks like a description of Etna, but 'is' is fodder and 'volatile' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatine is a rare radioactive chemical element, one of the halogens.

clue.text: Animal took a piece of food inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the letters sit within the run of words that comes before it

explanation.surface: A creature grabbed a morsel and swallowed it.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African mammal related to the giraffe.

parts.note: Orpheus was the legendary musician of Greek myth, so what he played was music of the classical world

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what songs the mythical lyre player knew.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpheus belongs to classical antiquity, so his songs are literally the music of the classical age.
